name: MoClo 2011 Level-0 module paths (body and declared fusion syntax)
scope: Original Figure 1B/C Level-0 role and fusion syntax for one declared four-module cytosolic or five-module signal-peptide path. Body-only checks for original BpiI entry and BsaI release, with advisory Esp3I readiness for later hierarchy. This is not vector or full transcription-unit compliance.
limitations: The declared module set must follow one complete four- or five-role path. This validates the selected syntax, not the biological identity, function or expression of each role.
Fusion labels are written along the assembled reference strand, not as reverse-complemented physical right-hand end labels. No actual cohesive termini, cleavage or ligation are inferred.

Inputs are explicit bodies only: additions are empty and the entire oriented sequence must be the declared body. BsaI/BpiI clamps, spacers, vector flanks and fusion-overlap bases are never invented or inserted.

AATG contains the original start-codon overlap; AGGT contains the signal-peptide/coding junction GGT. This profile checks neither body translation nor frame, start/stop codons, processing or targeting. It never prepends ATG or GGT.
Only the two separate-module paths in Figure 1B/C are admitted. Combined promoter/UTR modules, other composite modules, alternative tag syntax and Levels 1/2 or later overhangs remain unsupported.

BsaI and BpiI absence is required by this scoped original entry/release body policy. Esp3I absence is advisory for later hierarchical reuse, not a claim that an Esp3I site prevents an isolated BsaI-only Level-0-to-Level-1 assembly.

Only sequence motifs and declared grammar are checked. Circular destination vectors, source provenance, material isolation, reaction conditions, fidelity and experimental success require separate validation.
